item.title: GCC wants Constitution changed to ensure more women enter Parliament
item.description: The Great Council of Chiefs wants Fiji's next Constitution to guarantee more women a place in Parliament, saying it is time to move beyond promises and take action. In a statement, GCC Chairman Ratu Viliame Seruvakula says the Council is proposing a legislated quota requiring between 30 and 40 percent of Members of Parliament to be women.
item.content:encoded:
The Great Council of Chiefs wants Fiji's next Constitution to guarantee more women a place in Parliament, saying it is time to move beyond promises and take action.

In a statement, GCC Chairman Ratu Viliame Seruvakula says the Council is proposing a legislated quota requiring between 30 and 40 percent of Members of Parliament to be women.

He says any government elected after the 2027 General Election should no longer leave it to political parties to decide how many women they will field as candidates, with measures to improve women's representation instead written into the new Constitution.

Ratu Viliame says Fiji's current constitutional and electoral system has failed to create equal opportunities for women to participate in national and local governance, despite many capable and experienced women being ready to serve.

He says local government elections should also be used to develop future women leaders before they progress to national politics.

The GCC Chairman says many women want an electoral system that allows them to build direct relationships with their communities, be accountable to voters and earn election on their own merit.

He also says women have always played an important leadership role within the vanua , contributing to community development, preserving culture and supporting traditional obligations.

Ratu Viliame is urging the Prime Minister and the Government to support the Council's proposal, saying Fiji deserves a Constitution that gives all citizens an equal opportunity to serve their country.

item.title: Seaqaqa cane farmer to receive land lease next week after delay - TLTB
item.description: The iTaukei Land Trust Board says a Seaqaqa cane farmer who raised concerns about delays in receiving her land lease will receive the document next week. This follows concerns raised by cane farmer Sheila Wati during the Special Committee on the Sugar Industry's public consultation, where she said she had already paid the lease premium but was unable to start planting cane because she had not rece
item.content:encoded:
The iTaukei Land Trust Board says a Seaqaqa cane farmer who raised concerns about delays in receiving her land lease will receive the document next week.

This follows concerns raised by cane farmer Sheila Wati during the Special Committee on the Sugar Industry's public consultation, where she said she had already paid the lease premium but was unable to start planting cane because she had not received the lease.

Responding to questions by fijivillage News, TLTB Chief Executive Officer Solomone Nata says the lease has now been stamped by the Registrar of Titles in Suva and is being dispatched to Labasa today.

Nata says Wati is expected to receive the lease document next week.

He also apologised to the tenant for the delay.

When asked about the reason for the delay, Nata says the lease was lodged with the Registrar of Titles in May and has just been processed and returned.

Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka, who chairs the Special Committee on the Sugar Industry, had earlier requested Fiji Sugar Corporation Chief Executive Officer Bhan Singh to take Wati's details so that a response could be provided.

item.title: Legend FM and FM96 hosts prepare for Mount Batilamu challenge after 12-week wellness journey
item.description: Legend FM Breakfast Show hosts Alex Elbourne and Victoria Volmer, together with FM96 Breakfast Show hosts Joey Leilua, Tifa Vataiki and Elenoa Lido, will put their fitness to the test tomorrow when they climb Mount Batilamu, marking the final challenge of a 12-week workplace wellness programme. The Communications Fiji Limited personalities have been taking part in BSP Life's Healthy Choices Workpl
item.content:encoded:
Legend FM Breakfast Show hosts Alex Elbourne and Victoria Volmer, together with FM96 Breakfast Show hosts Joey Leilua, Tifa Vataiki and Elenoa Lido, will put their fitness to the test tomorrow when they climb Mount Batilamu, marking the final challenge of a 12-week workplace wellness programme.

The Communications Fiji Limited personalities have been taking part in BSP Life's Healthy Choices Workplace Wellness Programme, which encourages healthier lifestyles and aims to help reduce the growing impact of non-communicable diseases in Fiji.

Legend FM Content Director Victoria Volmer thanked BSP Life for supporting the team's wellness journey , saying the programme has helped participants build healthier habits while preparing them for the Mount Batilamu climb.

She says the team is excited and looking forward to completing the challenge together.

Speaking to fijivillage News ahead of the final challenge, BSP Life General Manager Distribution and Marketing George Kotobalavu says the Healthy Choices programme is being rolled out to corporate organisations across the country to promote health and wellbeing in the workplace.

Kotobalavu says the initiative encourages people to make healthier choices in their everyday lives, whether it is eating nutritious meals, exercising regularly or simply staying active.

He says Fiji continues to face a major challenge with non-communicable diseases, and BSP Life wants to take a proactive approach by helping people adopt healthier habits.

Kotobalavu says the Healthy Choices programme is about raising awareness, encouraging discipline and supporting people to live longer, healthier lives.

item.title: Union claims EFL executives received higher pay as workers await wage increases
item.description: Concerns have been raised after workers at Energy Fiji Limited represented by the Construction Energy and Timber Workers Union of Fiji claims they have gone three years without a wage increase while senior executives have received higher remuneration. In a statement, the union claims recent figures show the total remuneration for EFL's Chief Executive Officer and Executive Management Group increas
item.content:encoded:
Concerns have been raised after workers at Energy Fiji Limited represented by the Construction Energy and Timber Workers Union of Fiji claims they have gone three years without a wage increase while senior executives have received higher remuneration.

In a statement, the union claims recent figures show the total remuneration for EFL's Chief Executive Officer and Executive Management Group increased from $3.309 million in 2024 to $3.756 million in 2025 .

The union says its members are still waiting for wage increases for 2024, 2025 and 2026, alleging that EFL has not settled the union's log of claims for those years.

They say the difference in pay raises raises concerns about fairness and equitable treatment of workers, arguing that employees who contribute to EFL's operations should also be fairly compensated.

The union says rewarding senior management while delaying wage settlements for union members affects staff morale and undermines trust.

They are calling on EFL to enter into what it describes as genuine, good-faith negotiations to resolve the outstanding wage claims and reach a fair outcome for its members.

The union says it remains committed to constructive industrial relations but believes wage increases should be distributed fairly and consistently across the organisation rather than benefiting only senior management.

They are also urging EFL's Board and executive leadership to begin negotiations without delay and settle the outstanding claims.

We have sent questions to Energy Fiji Limited.

item.title: Search continues for 6 missing at sea as MSAF urges mariners to heed weather warnings
item.description: As the search continues for the 6 people who were travelling in a fibre glass boat between Namuka and Fulaga in the Lau Group, m ariners in maritme areas across Fiji are being urged to strictly follow active weather warnings. item.content:encoded:
As the search continues for the 6 people who were travelling in a fibre glass boat between Namuka and Fulaga in the Lau Group, m ariners in maritme areas across Fiji are being urged to strictly follow active weather warnings.

According to reports received by MSAF, the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) Fiji was notified yesterday that a half-cabin fibre glass boat powered by a 40-horsepower outboard engine had failed to arrive at its destination.

The vessel reportedly departed Namuka Island at around 10am yesterday bound for Fulaga Island.

Three fibre glass boats left Namuka that morning while two arrived safely in Fulaga, the third remains overdue with six people on board.

Following the report, JRCC Fiji, operating from the Vuvale Maritime Essential Services Centre (MESC), immediately activated search and rescue operations.

Navy Search and Rescue (SAR) mission coordinators have been working through the night, coordinating with government agencies, nearby vessels, and community contacts across the area.

Plans are underway to deploy both sea and air search assets today to widen the search effort.

Authorities are concerned that the missing vessel may not have been carrying essential life-saving equipment.

They say search operations are also being made more difficult by deteriorating weather conditions, including strong winds and rough to very rough seas.

They say despite these challenges, every effort remains focused on locating the vessel and bringing its occupants to safety.

M SAF is asking all mariners travelling between Namuka, Fulaga, and surrounding waters to keep a vigilant lookout for a white half-cabin fibreglass boat powered by a 40-horsepowe r outboard engine and its six occupants.

Anyone who sights the vessel or has information that could assist the search is urged to contact JRCC Fiji immediately on the toll-free number 1539 or report it to the nearest Police Station .

MSAF also reminds all mariners to take the nationwide Strong Wind Warning, issued on Thursday, 6 August 2026, seriously. The warning advises of southeasterly winds of 20 to 30 knots and rough to very rough sea conditions across affected areas.

In light of this incident, MSAF is reminding vessel owners and small-boat operators of their responsibilities to ensure safe operations at sea.

The search remains active, and further updates will be provided through official channels as confirmed information becomes available.
